stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key ML domains including transformers, llama, and text-generation.
This indicates active community interest and benchmarking activity around Meta's latest LLM releases.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model released under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and features native support for image input accelerated by Ollama's MLX engine.

stories.title: Meta’s $25 billion legal loss just put blood in the water
stories.author: Lauren Feiner
bullet_points: Meta faces a massive $25 billion legal penalty following a ruling by a New Mexico judge.
The ruling significantly surpasses a previous $17 billion settlement reached with US attorneys general.
The lawsuit centers on allegations that Meta misled users regarding its practices around 2018.

stories.title: Google’s next Genie AI model generates more realistic experiences
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Google unveiled Genie 4, a new world model designed to generate highly realistic, interactive AI experiences.
Key features include real-time experience modification via natural language prompts and integrated audio generation.
The model leverages Gemini 3.8 Flash as its underlying technology.

stories.title: Apple is adding an AI chatbot to Pages, Keynote, and Numbers
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Apple is integrating an AI assistant into its core productivity suite (Pages, Keynote, Numbers).
The assistant leverages AI models from both Apple and OpenAI to understand document context.
Key functionalities include automated design, animation, drafting, and content refinement within the apps.

stories.title: 155 responses leaked between AI customers: the GLM-5.3 KV cache bug — and the canary test for YOUR provider
stories.author: slabb
bullet_points: A critical data leak was discovered on Cloudflare Workers AI involving the GLM-5.3 model.
The vulnerability stemmed from a stale KV-cache bug, leading to other customers' responses being served to users.
The article details the technical reproduction steps and provides a canary script for users to test their AI providers for similar cross-request leaks.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on the Hugging Face platform.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The model is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30-billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for running complex, multi-step tasks and tool-calling locally on user hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Anthropic’s elaborate plan to keep Wall Street at bay
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: Anthropic is preparing for an IPO, aiming to access public market capital.
The company faces a tension between maximizing shareholder returns and maintaining its core mission of safe AI development.
The increasing capability of their AI models introduces greater inherent risks that must be managed.

stories.title: Microsoft offers to buy out a quarter of its workforce
stories.author: Nick Indge
bullet_points: Microsoft is reportedly offering voluntary buyout packages to a portion of its global workforce.
The affected employees are located across the US, Canada, India, and the UK.
This signals potential organizational restructuring or workforce optimization within the tech giant.

stories.title: Retriever-Free Retrieval: Navigating Documents with Decision Models
stories.author: Kilian Q. Weinberger
bullet_points: Addresses a critical limitation in current LLM workflows where retrieval failures limit generator performance.
Introduces DecisionRAG, a novel approach that integrates language model capabilities into the retrieval phase.
Achieves retrieval evaluation using decision models in a single forward pass, avoiding token generation overhead.

stories.title: Patient-specific rubric-based evaluation of large language models across longitudinal cancer care
stories.author: Ying Sun
bullet_points: Introduces NPC-RubricBench, a new benchmark for evaluating LLMs in longitudinal cancer care.
Addresses a gap in current LLM evaluations by moving beyond isolated clinical encounters to track care across entire patient pathways.
Uses nasopharyngeal carcinoma data from 405 patients to test multistage clinical reasoning capabilities of LLMs.

stories.title: Reva: Real-Time Vulnerability Detection through Contextual Probing of Large Language Models
stories.author: Massih-Reza Amini
bullet_points: Introduces 'Reva,' a system designed for real-time vulnerability detection in rapidly generated code.
Leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) to act as security experts by performing contextual probing and hypothesis testing.
Addresses the critical industry problem of software vulnerabilities being more costly when discovered late in the development cycle.

stories.title: Pretraining Knows What, Simulation Teaches How: Compositional Generalization in a Sim-Trained Robot Agent
stories.author: Shyamal Buch
bullet_points: Introduces Zero-real Agent Policy (ZAP) to bridge the gap between world understanding and robotic action.
Leverages a large pretrained vision-language model (27B parameters) for initial world reasoning.
Uses simulation (supervised fine-tuning and GRPO) to teach the model the necessary physical control skills.

stories.title: Pretraining Knows What, Simulation Teaches How: Compositional Generalization in a Sim-Trained Robot Agent
stories.author: Shyamal Buch
bullet_points: Introduces Zero-real Agent Policy (ZAP) to bridge the gap between world understanding and robotic action.
Leverages large pretrained vision-language models (27B parameters) for initial world reasoning.
Uses simulation-based fine-tuning (supervised fine-tuning and GRPO) to teach the model physical control.

stories.title: Speech models in Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has expanded its capabilities to include support for speech models.
The initial supported model is Phonon from Gradium, enabling text-to-speech functionality.
The feature offers fast, real-time streaming of speech in five languages, achieving over 100x real-time speed on Apple Silicon.

stories.title: Clef is available on Ollama's cloud
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Clef, a 27B multimodal decision model from Cloudflare, is now integrated with Ollama.
Users have the option to run the Clef model either locally or via Ollama's cloud infrastructure.
This integration expands the capabilities of Ollama by adding a powerful, multimodal model.

stories.title: Reflection's Beam is freely available on Ollama for a limited time
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Reflection's open-weight model, Beam, is now available on Ollama.
Beam is specifically designed for software engineering, reasoning, and agentic tasks.
The model is offered for free for a limited time via Ollama Cloud.

stories.title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama enables the use of its cloud models for AI agents.
The integration allows these AI agents to run safely within Fly.io's cloud infrastructure.
This combination addresses the need for secure deployment of AI agents in a cloud environment.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free execution of decision-making processes.
Decision models can process text to provide probabilistic answers for yes/no questions, choices, or scores.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to leverage open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-weight model ecosystems.

stories.title: Firefox’s Smart Window adds AI form filling and webpage monitoring
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Firefox is enhancing its Smart Window feature with new AI capabilities.
The update allows the browser to auto-fill online forms by pulling data from open tabs.
Use cases include automatically populating job applications using information from profiles like LinkedIn.

stories.title: US officials want Section 702 renewed before damaging court ruling goes public
stories.author: Dell Cameron, wired.com
bullet_points: US officials are pushing to renew Section 702 of surveillance laws.
There are allegations that officials concealed a court ruling regarding warrantless searches until after its public release deadline.
The story touches upon significant issues of government surveillance and legal oversight.

stories.title: Apple reveals updated iPad mini with a bigger OLED screen for $700
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Apple has released an updated iPad mini.
The key hardware upgrade is a larger OLED screen.
The new model is priced at $700 and is touted as a major line update.

stories.title: Learning Force-Reactive Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
stories.author: Haozhi Qi
bullet_points: Introduces FLORE, a new framework for learning force-reactive locomotion and manipulation in humanoids.
Addresses the challenge that real-world tasks require controlling contact forces, not just kinematic trajectories.
Utilizes robot-free demonstrations captured via force-sensing grippers and wearable body trackers.

stories.title: I-HITL: Inalienable Human-in-the-Loop
stories.author: Ari Juels
bullet_points: Addresses the growing vulnerability of traditional Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) systems against advanced AI agents.
Introduces the concept of Inalienable Human-in-the-Loop (I-HITL) to enforce mandatory human approval for AI actions.
Focuses on robustly ensuring that AI agents cannot execute critical actions without explicit human consent.

stories.title: Profiling a Frontier Agent with EBench: From Direct Control to Harness with Policy
stories.author: Chunhua Shen
bullet_points: The research evaluates frontier multimodal LLMs (like GPT-6-Astra) for robot control without requiring robot-specific training.
It focuses on comparing the capabilities of these LLMs against established Vision-Language-Action (VLA) and World Action Model (WAM) policies.
The evaluation is conducted using the EBench framework under standardized visual and proprioceptive observation protocols.

stories.title: Learning When to Commit: Schedule Distillation for Fast Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Zhiqiang Shen
bullet_points: Addresses the inefficiency of Diffusion Large Language Models (dLLMs) which require many decoding rounds for response generation.
Proposes 'dSpark,' a schedule distillation method to improve generation efficiency by optimizing when the model commits to tokens.
Highlights that the utility of a token depends not just on its predictability, but on how it aids in predicting subsequent, less predictable positions.

stories.title: Game theory of academic effort and hiring in the age of AI
stories.author: Peter S. Park
bullet_points: The rise of accessible AI challenges traditional academic evaluation methods.
AI makes producing high-quality, theoretically sound research papers cheaper.
This lowers the reliability of research output as a signal for academic expertise.

stories.title: Auto-Research Arena: Benchmarking and Advancing Auto-Research in Language Modeling
stories.author: Hanwen Jiang
bullet_points: Introduces 'Auto-Research Arena,' a new multi-target benchmark for evaluating autonomous research systems in language modeling.
The benchmark is designed to support meaningful research progress by separating result admissibility from actual improvement.
It allows for testing diverse research objectives within a shared experimental environment, considering model quality and resource constraints.

stories.title: Learning Force-Reactive Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
stories.author: Haozhi Qi
bullet_points: Introduces FLORE, a new framework for learning force-reactive locomotion and manipulation in humanoids.
Addresses the complexity of tasks requiring coordinated contact force control across hands and the body, which kinematics alone cannot solve.
Utilizes robot-free demonstrations captured via force-sensing grippers and wearable body trackers.

stories.title: Work Agents: Systems, Capabilities, and Optimization
stories.author: Weiwen Liu
bullet_points: The research addresses the growing capability of AI agents to move from information generation to digital work execution.
It identifies a gap in current research regarding a unified perspective on how agents reliably complete complex, delegated tasks.
The paper proposes a work-centric, system-level view, modeling agents as systems combining foundation models with runtime harnesses.

stories.title: Does VGGT Know What It Does Not Know?
stories.author: David Nordström
bullet_points: The research investigates the uncertainty estimation capabilities of 3D reconstruction models like VGGT, which currently output deterministic predictions.
The study tests if the model's internal features can implicitly signal when its predicted camera poses are incorrect, even without explicit uncertainty reporting.
Using a linear probe on frozen VGGT features, the authors successfully predict pose failure on a difficult benchmark set (HardMatch) where the model fails 35% of the time.

stories.title: Learning When to Commit: Schedule Distillation for Fast Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Zhiqiang Shen
bullet_points: Addresses the inefficiency of Diffusion Large Language Models (dLLMs) which require many decoding rounds.
Proposes 'dSpark,' a schedule distillation method to improve generation speed.
Focuses on optimizing the commitment strategy—deciding when to commit to a token based on its predictive utility for future tokens.

stories.title: FOCUS: Active Critic Learning for Long-Horizon Language Model Agents
stories.author: Benjamin Van Durme
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of sparse outcome rewards in long-horizon language model agents.
Introduces FOCUS, a Reinforcement Learning (RL) method designed to improve critic network accuracy.
FOCUS mitigates high computational costs associated with estimating intermediate state values via selective branching.

stories.title: Preserve to Expand: Source-Aware Adaptation and Model Merging for Multilingual LLM-Based ASR
stories.author: Ravi Shekhar
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of expanding multilingual Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems to new languages.
Proposes using a 'connector-based Speech LLM' architecture where a trainable connector maps speech representations to a frozen LLM.
Investigates target-update construction and model merging strategies to adapt the connector while preserving performance on previously supported languages.

stories.title: Learning When to Commit: Schedule Distillation for Fast Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Zhiqiang Shen
bullet_points: Introduces dSpark, a new schedule distillation method for Diffusion Large Language Models (dLLMs).
Addresses the inefficiency in dLLMs caused by requiring many decoding rounds for token generation.
Proposes that efficient generation depends on strategically committing to tokens, balancing predictability with contextual gain.

stories.title: Quantifying Claim Smoothing by LLM Research Agents
stories.author: Greg Durrett
bullet_points: LLMs synthesizing information from large document collections can produce reports that sound confident but are factually inaccurate.
The research identifies a phenomenon called 'claim smoothing,' where LLMs collapse diverse or conflicting source material into a single, overly smooth narrative.
This smoothing process causes the model to discard the necessary 'evidential jaggedness' present in the underlying source documents.

stories.title: SEMA-Auto: Sighted and Efficient Multi-Turn Attack with Autonomy
stories.author: Jianfeng Gao
bullet_points: Introduces SEMA-Auto, a new framework designed to improve multi-turn adversarial attacks (jailbreaking) against LLMs.
Addresses limitations of existing methods: static planners lack context, while interactive generators are computationally expensive due to required in-loop evaluators.
SEMA-Auto aims to bridge this gap by offering a 'sighted and efficient' approach to multi-turn attack generation.

stories.title: Can JEV Support Clinical Trial Criteria Assessment?
stories.author: Wu Yuan
bullet_points: The research investigates the capability of JEV, a non-generative decision model, to assess clinical trial criteria from patient records.
It compares JEV against schema-constrained Qwen Flash using datasets derived from MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV.
The study focuses on the critical task of distinguishing unmet conditions from insufficient evidence in patient data.

stories.title: Quantitative Generalization Bounds for Multi-Layer Transformers: A Few Long Strings can Beat Many Short Ones
stories.author: Michael Hahn
bullet_points: The paper addresses the theoretical gap in understanding how Transformer models generalize to complex, long-instance problems.
It proposes quantitative generalization bounds, suggesting a deeper mathematical framework for Transformer capabilities.
The research highlights that Transformer generalization requires analyzing both in-distribution statistical generalization and other factors.

stories.title: From Self-Confidence to Statistical Accuracy: Scaling Human-in-the-Loop Evaluation with Direct and LLM-Assisted Auditing
stories.author: Yang Zhou
bullet_points: Addresses the issue of miscalibrated self-confidence in LLMs and MLLMs, suggesting it can still be useful for evaluation.
Proposes a unified statistical framework to compare and leverage both direct human auditing and LLM-as-a-judge methods.
Analyzes the trade-offs between direct auditing (human effort) and LLM-as-a-judge (cost/calibration quality) for scalable evaluation.

stories.title: JetBrains open-sourced an agentic IDE where agents never touch your checkout
stories.author: slabb
bullet_points: JetBrains has open-sourced Thinkrail, an agentic IDE under Apache-2.0.
The architecture isolates agent operations by placing each agent in its own git worktree.
The project uses a graph of SPEC.md files to maintain its state, emphasizing decentralized, account-free operation.
